item.title: Korea’s DongSin EF plans $1.8B green ammonia investment in Vietnam’s Lam Dong province
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam's Lam Dong province is considering a proposal by South Korea's DongSin EF to build a green ammonia project costing about $1.78 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam’s Lam Dong province is considering a proposal by South Korea’s DongSin EF to build a green ammonia project costing about $1.78 billion.

In a statement on Wednesday, Lam Dong People’s Committee said the South Korean firm made the proposal at a meeting with Deputy Chairman of the provincial People’s Committee Nguyen Ba Ut.

The company proposes an integrated plant combining a solar farm, water electrolysis, an ammonia synthesis complex, storage, and export facilities. The site would be in the Tuy Phong solar development area, about 18 kilometers from Vinh Tan port.

In phase one, the plant would produce 300,000 tons of green ammonia a year. It has a total investment of $1.782 billion, including construction, equipment, and financing costs during construction. The company said it hopes to raise capacity to 1.2 million tons a year over the long term. It plans to use solar power first and study wind power later.

Later phases would depend on the results of phase one, market commitments and the company’s financial capacity.

According to the company’s governance adviser, Na Dong Heon, the project is still at the research stage and is receiving funding from the South Korean government. The company wanted the provincial authorities to advise on the next steps, he added.

In reply, Ut said Lam Dong has strong potential for renewable energy, particularly wind and solar. Green hydrogen and ammonia projects fit national energy policy and the province’s development direction.

Officials said the proposal is consistent with Vietnam’s National Green Growth Strategy, its Hydrogen Energy Development Strategy and the adjusted Power Development Plan VIII.

item.title: Indonesia’s sovereign fund Danantara posts $14B net profit in 2025
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Danantara Indonesia recorded a net profit of Rp203.4 trillion ($14 billion) for the nine-month period in its first consolidated financial statements for the 2025 financial year.
item.content:encoded:
Danantara Indonesia recorded a net profit of Rp203.4 trillion ($14 billion) for the nine-month period in its first consolidated financial statements for the 2025 financial year.

The net profit reflects nine months of portfolio performance following the in-kind transfer of State-Owned Enterprise (SOE) shares in March 2025, and is supported by operating revenue of Rp2,385.2 trillion and net cash flow from operating activities of Rp563.1 trillion, the firm said in a statement on Wednesday.

This performance strengthens Danantara Indonesia’s capacity to drive national economic growth through SOE transformation and investment in productive sectors.

As of December 31, 2025, its total consolidated assets stood at Rp11,607 trillion. Meanwhile, on a 12-month pro forma basis, return on equity (ROE) reached 8.7 percent.

Danantara Indonesia Chief Executive Officer Rosan Roeslani said the results demonstrate the strength and productivity of the portfolio managed by Danantara Indonesia.

“For the first time, the performance of Danantara Indonesia’s entire portfolio is presented in a single set of audited consolidated financial statements,

“The results show a portfolio of significant scale, capable of generating healthy profitability and cash flow, and contributing to national economic activity. This foundation is our starting point to continue improving asset productivity and creating long-term value for Indonesia,” he added.

For the audited consolidation period from April to December 2025, Danantara Indonesia recorded operating revenue of Rp2,385.2 trillion and net profit of Rp203.4 trillion. Net cash flow from operating activities reached Rp563.1 trillion, while the debt-to-equity ratio was maintained at 0.54 times.

Financing and investment activity also increased, with loans and financing receivables growing 7.2 percent to Rp3,998.9 trillion and investments in securities rising 11.1 percent to Rp1,485.9 trillion.

The Danantara Indonesia ecosystem also paid Rp567.2 trillion in taxes in 2025, while State Capital Participation (PMN) allocations declined from Rp54.6 trillion in 2022 to Rp4.7 trillion in 2025.

“Danantara Indonesia’s success is measured not only by the size of its assets, but by its ability to make them more productive, generate sustainable returns and deliver real impact for the economy. Investment discipline, SOE transformation and governance will remain our priorities in the years ahead,” Rosan said.

Danantara Indonesia said it is following a phased roadmap to build the institution, strengthen its capabilities and sustain long-term value creation.

Having laid its institutional foundations in 2025, the fund is entering a phase of expanded transformation in 2026–2027.

The focus is on business transformation and restructuring across its portfolio companies, portfolio diversification, consistent returns, and a stronger capital structure and talent ecosystem.

In 2028–2029, Danantara Indonesia said it will focus on building Indonesia Global Champions in strategic sectors and strengthening its position as a world-class sovereign fund.

In support of national down streaming, the fund has begun developing more than 20 down streaming projects worth approximately Rp225 trillion across energy, minerals and metals, and food and agro-industry.

SOE transformation through Danantara Asset Management (DAM) also continued to accelerate. As of October 2026, 364 of approximately 1,074 SOE entities had been streamlined toward a target of 250–300 entities, with potential efficiencies of up to Rp50 trillion a year.

Performance improvements are beginning to show, including Garuda Indonesia adding 20 serviceable aircraft to reach 104 as of September 2026, and Krakatau Steel turning a $105.38 million loss in the first half of 2025 into a $10.94 million profit in the first half of 2026.

DAM has also driven the consolidation of Pertamina’s downstream businesses, as well as the establishment of Danareksa Investments, formed through the merger of four SOE investment management companies with more than Rp170 trillion in assets under management.

On the investment side, Danantara Investment Management (DIM) is targeting $3.8 billion in private investments to be deployed and signed in 2026.

As of October 2026, total investment assets stood at approximately Rp162 trillion, including Rp60.6 trillion in public investments.

Several strategic investments have moved into execution. The national Waste-to-Energy (PSEL) program across 33 regencies/cities is valued at approximately Rp40–50 trillion, with DIM’s investment of around Rp10 trillion serving as a catalyst.

DIM has also strengthened the Hajj and Umrah ecosystem through the acquisition of the 1,461-room Novotel Thakher Makkah and 4.4 hectares of land; invested in the Chlor Alkali–Ethylene Dichloride (CA-EDC) project, which is approximately 80 percent constructed; and signed an investment for a 25 percent stake in JBS’s protein business in Australia and New Zealand.

Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir says Indonesian corporate fundamentals remain strong despite market concerns

item.title: Catcha Digital’s net profit jumps more than two folds to $1.67M in Q3 on higher revenue
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Malaysia's technology firm Catcha Digital Berhad has reported two times jump in its net profit to MYR 6.88 million ($1.67 million) in the third quarter ended 31 December, 2026 amid an increase in revenue.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia’s technology firm Catcha Digital Berhad has reported two times jump in its net profit to MYR 6.88 million ($1.67 million) in the third quarter ended 31 December, 2026 amid an increase in revenue.

The firm’s revenue for the quarter surged 69.44 percent year on year to MYR 42.8 million ringgit, mainly driven by higher experiential advertising and digital advertising revenue, it said in a statement on Wednesday.

As for the first nine months ended September 30, 2026, the firm’s net profit slipped 11.25 percent year on year to MYR 5.18 million while its revenue soared 90.41 percent year on year to MYR 90.49 million.

“We are deeply inspired by Berkshire Hathaway to be the permanent home for market-leading companies in Southeast Asia. We acquire these companies, work with their founders to grow them organically, and reinvest the cash flow generated into the next acquisition,

“This quarter showed that the flywheel has started spinning and delivered our biggest quarter ever both in revenue and profits,” said Eric Tan, Group Chief Executive Officer of Catcha Digital.

All three flagship expos, Agri Malaysia, MBAM OneBuild and the Malaysian International Food and Beverage Exhibition (MIFB), were held in the third quarter, the segment’s peak quarter.

The firm’s cash and cash equivalents were MYR 31.70 million at September 30, 2026, against bank borrowings of MYR 12.29 million under a MYR 35 million revolving credit facility with Affin Hwang Investment Bank Berhad. Up to MYR 73.9 million more is available from outstanding warrants as a reserve source.

The firm highlighted that its growth is funded first from free cash flow and vendor financing, then debt, then equity.

“Nine months into 2026, the Catcha Digital platform is compounding as we intended. With eight acquisitions now contributing across three verticals, we expect a meaningfully stronger FY2026 than FY2025,

“We will continue to pursue strategic partnerships, investments and acquisitions that are directly accretive to our earnings per share,” said Patrick Grove, Chairman of Catcha Digital.

Catcha Digital said it has completed eight acquisitions since 2025, each positioned to strengthen its foothold in the digital media, business to business (B2B) expo and information technology (IT) solutions space, all expected to contribute positively to future earnings. No new acquisitions were completed during the third quarter of FY2026.

Malaysia’s Catcha Digital slips into the red despite higher revenue

item.title: ZTE partners True Corp to unveil TDD dual-band AAU solution in Thailand
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: ZTE Corporation, a Chinese provider of integrated information and communication technology solutions, has partnered with True Corporation, Thailand's telecom-tech company, to deploy a TDD dual-band AAU solution for 5G-Advanced and future evolution.
item.content:encoded:
ZTE Corporation, a Chinese provider of integrated information and communication technology solutions, has partnered with True Corporation, Thailand’s telecom-tech company, to deploy a TDD dual-band AAU solution for 5G-Advanced and future evolution.

Designed for high integration, wide coverage, large capacity, and lower power consumption, the solution is intended to enhance network quality and efficiency and provide wireless support for individual users, industry digitalization, and computing power networks, the duo said in a statement.

As Thailand’s digital economy accelerates, with explosive traffic growth, wider adoption of AI-capable devices, and deeper industry applications, wireless networks now face rising demands for bandwidth, latency, coverage, and energy performance.

TRUE continues to advance its premium network construction, while ZTE remains focused on innovation in wireless access and Massive MIMO.

In this collaboration, TRUE specified the performance targets based on its network requirements, and ZTE customized the A9651D M2326 accordingly.

Following joint single-site and first-cluster POC test validation, the equipment has been deployed at scale in TRUE’s network. This deployment reflects the technical collaboration between TRUE and ZTE to improve network performance and energy efficiency.

According to the results of joint field tests conducted in TRUE’s network, large-scale antenna arrays and intelligent beamforming enable the A9651D M2326 to achieve a 116 percent improvement in 2.6 GHz traffic compared with data measured before the first-cluster POC site test, attain 1.7Gbps throughput via SA NR CA (700+2300+2600), and successfully enable LTE 7CC CA.

By consolidating two TDD bands into a single AAU, the solution can reduce TDD RF units by 57 percent and overall weight by 30 percent compared with deploying separate single-band units, enabling rapid deployment across urban, suburban, and all other scenarios.

On energy efficiency, ZTE’s innovative Super-N2.0 solution enhances PA efficiency.

According to the field test results, after upgrading to the new equipment, site energy consumption was reduced by 11 percent compared with deploying separate single-band units.

It enables low-carbon operation while ensuring performance, helping operators pursue global decarbonization objectives such as net-zero targets and science‑based emissions reductions, and reducing long-term operating costs.

The solution supports one-step TDD deployment and is positioned for future spectrum evolution and 5G-Advanced new features and solutions, delivering long-term benefits from a single deployment.

This collaboration supports TRUE’s network requirements through equipment customization, joint testing, and commercial deployment, said the statement.

Malaysia’s U Mobile, ZTE test three-day off-grid 5G deployment in East Malaysia

item.title: Petronas, Tokyo Gas advance partnership with first bio-LNG delivery from Malaysia to Japan
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas), through its wholly owned subsidiary Petronas LNG Ltd. (PLL), has successfully delivered its maiden International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) PLUS-certified Bio-LNG from Malaysia to Japan in partnership with Tokyo Gas Co., Ltd. (Tokyo Gas), marking a significant milestone in advancing a renewable gas pathway between the two companies.
item.content:encoded:
Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas), through its wholly owned subsidiary Petronas LNG Ltd. (PLL), has successfully delivered its maiden International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) PLUS-certified Bio-LNG from Malaysia to Japan in partnership with Tokyo Gas Co., Ltd. (Tokyo Gas), marking a significant milestone in advancing a renewable gas pathway between the two companies.

The milestone follows the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by Petronas and Tokyo Gas on October 27, 2026 to expand collaboration across the LNG value chain and explore decarbonization opportunities, Petronas said in a statement.

Beyond the long-standing partnership, the Bio-LNG delivery also demonstrates the progression into practical solutions, combining Petronas’ integrated LNG capabilities with Tokyo Gas’ commitment to advancing lower-carbon energy solutions.

The successful delivery also supports Tokyo Gas’ efforts to contribute towards Japan’s ambition of introducing 1 percent of renewable gas, including e-methane and biomethane into its city gas by 2030.

Bringing together expertise across the Petronas Group, the first Bio-LNG cargo was co-loaded with conventional LNG at the Regasification Terminal Pengerang (RGTP) in Johor.

Sourced by PLL through Petronas Energy & Gas Trading Sdn. Bhd. (PEGT), the palm oil mill effluent (POME)-based Bio-LNG was delivered through Petronas’ established LNG infrastructure operated by PETRONAS Gas Berhad (PGB), demonstrating the Group’s integrated capabilities to deliver lower-carbon energy solutions.

“This milestone demonstrates Petronas’ strength across the LNG value chain, leveraging biomethane sourcing, existing infrastructure, commercial capabilities and market access to deliver alternative solutions such as Bio-LNG,

“By combining Malaysia’s biomethane potential with the scale, reliability and market reach of our established LNG portfolio, we are creating pathways for renewable gas to reach international markets while continuing to provide the energy security our customers depend on,” Petronas Executive Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of Gas & Maritime Business, Adif Zulkifli said。

“It also represents an important step forward in our longstanding partnership with Tokyo Gas. Working closely together to validate the Bio-LNG supply chain requirements has been instrumental in enabling its successful delivery from Malaysia to Japan,

“We look forward to building on this strong foundation to advance practical decarbonization solutions that address customers’ evolving energy needs and support growing demand for lower-carbon energy solutions in the region,” he added.

This delivery also reflects Petronas’ continued efforts to advance its Energy Transition Strategy and pathway towards achieving Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2050, while pursuing new growth opportunities in cleaner and lower-carbon energy solutions, said the statement.

Petronas, TotalEnergies, Mitsui ink deal to develop carbon storage area in Southern CCS Hub

item.title: Vietnam’s Viettel, Singapore’s Singtel break ground on 600 Tbps international subsea cable
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Viettel and Singtel, two major telecommunications of Vietnam and Singapore, have kicked off the construction of the Vietnam–Thailand-Singapore submarine cable project (VTS) linking three Southeast Asian nations.
item.content:encoded:
Viettel and Singtel, two major telecommunications of Vietnam and Singapore, have kicked off the construction of the Vietnam–Thailand-Singapore submarine cable project (VTS) linking three Southeast Asian nations.

In a statement on Thursday, Viettel said the project is the first international subsea cable initiated and owned by a Vietnamese company. The cable is about 2,500 kilometres long, with a design capacity of 600 Tbps. It is is expected to complete in the fourth quarter of 2030.

The Vietnam–Singapore section is about 1,200 kilometers long and designed for 240 Tbps. This speed is about 2.5 times the combined capacity of Vietnam’s current international cables.

Viettel said the route is the shortest between Vietnam and Singapore and the cable will use eight fiber pairs and new wavelength-division multiplexing technology. It expects round-trip latency of about 12 milliseconds, about 50 percent lower than the average of existing routes.

Viettel chairman and CEO Tao Duc Thang said building a submarine cable takes many years but “we cannot wait until capacity is short before investing.” Viettel said it leads route planning and design, which determine the landing points and configuration of the system.

Vietnamese Deputy Minister of Science and Technology Pham Duc Long said the project marks a shift from mainly using to actively helping build international connectivity infrastructure.

Truong Minh Huy Vu, vice chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People’s Committee, said the landing station in the city “opens a direct gateway to Singapore.” Ho Chi Minh City will include the cable project in its digital infrastructure planning.

Keith Leong, Singtel’s deputy group chief executive for enterprise, said: “Building new routes keeps data flowing even when existing connections are disrupted.”

The project will also feature Thailand’s AIS, VNPT, FPT Telecom and Viettel IDC. The contractors are NEC Corporation of Japan and ASEAN Cableship of Singapore.

Vietnam’s FPT Telecom to invest in Vietnam–Singapore submarine cable VTS

item.title: Kingsoft operating profit rises 40 percent as AI businesses grow
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Kingsoft reported 40 percent operating profit growth as its WPS office business and associate Kingsoft Cloud expanded AI-related revenue.
item.content:encoded:
Hong Kong-listed software and games company Kingsoft Corporation reported a 40 percent year-on-year increase in operating profit for the third quarter, as growth in its smart office business and associate Kingsoft Cloud offset slower momentum elsewhere.

Kingsoft said group revenue reached RMB 2.44 billion ($343 million) in the three months ended September 30, up 1 percent from a year earlier. Operating profit was RMB 388 million, while adjusted net profit attributable to owners of the parent increased 12 percent to RMB 300 million.

The company had about RMB 27.5 billion in cash resources at the end of the quarter. Kingsoft said its AI-enabled businesses were the main driver of revenue growth, attributing part of the performance to AI product rollouts and continued investment in research and development.

Revenue from the smart office segment increased 16 percent to RMB 1.77 billion. Within the segment, the WPS individual business generated RMB 1.05 billion, up 17 percent, while WPS 365 revenue rose 34 percent to RMB 270 million. WPS software revenue increased 6 percent to RMB 414 million.

WPS Office had 678 million monthly active devices worldwide as of September 30, an increase of 1.3 percent from a year earlier. Kingsoft said AI features helped raise paid conversion and average revenue per user in its individual office business, although it did not disclose separate user or revenue figures for the AI products.

The online games and other businesses generated RMB 672 million in revenue. Kingsoft said it had adjusted commercialization schedules and reallocated internal resources, without providing a year-on-year comparison for the segment in its release.

Associate company Kingsoft Cloud reported quarterly revenue of RMB 3.48 billion, up 40 percent year on year. AI cloud billing revenue reached RMB 1.68 billion, a 115 percent increase, while adjusted operating margin rose to 4.4 percent.

Kingsoft said it plans to continue integrating AI across office applications, interactive entertainment and cloud infrastructure, while expanding cooperation between the Kingsoft and Xiaomi ecosystems.

Kingsoft Cloud Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

item.title: Malaysia’s regulator sues Google over harmful YouTube content, seeks $146M in damages
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has filed two lawsuits against Google LLC over its alleged failure to address harmful content on YouTube, seeking a combined MYR 600 million ($145.76 million) in damages as part of efforts to protect children and the public from online threats.
item.content:encoded:
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has filed two lawsuits against Google LLC over its alleged failure to address harmful content on YouTube, seeking a combined MYR 600 million ($145.76 million) in damages as part of efforts to protect children and the public from online threats.

The regulator said in a statement that it is seeking MYR 300 million in damages for each lawsuit, comprising MYR 100 million in general damages, MYR 100 million in aggravated damages and MYR 100 million in exemplary damages.

The claims are intended to compensate for the substantial resources and manpower deployed to address more than 50,000 instances of harmful online content following what the commission described as Google’s systemic failures.

They also seek to hold the company accountable and prevent similar non-compliance from recurring.

The first lawsuit concerns Google’s alleged failure to take appropriate action against thousands of instances of harmful content on YouTube, including online gambling, scams and fraud.

Between Jan 1 and Oct 28, 2026, MCMC submitted 74,703 reports to YouTube, of which 74,569, or 99.8 percent, were related to online gambling.

Of the online gambling-related reports, 32,781 received a response or resulted in content removal within one day, while 4,950 received no response.

Another 35 reports took more than 90 days to receive a response or result in content removal, while 1,468 took more than 30 days from the date they were submitted.

These figures highlight the scale of harmful content circulating on the platform and delays in addressing such material, MCMC said.

The second lawsuit involves Google’s alleged failure to take appropriate statutory and proactive measures against the republication of unlawful content on YouTube by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo.

The content is currently subject to an interim injunction granted by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on June 19, 2026.

MCMC said its claims in the two cases were based on alleged breaches of statutory provisions, relevant licensing conditions and negligence.

The commission stressed that all social media platform providers subject to the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and the Online Safety Act 2025 must comply with their respective legal obligations and licensing conditions.

It also urged all platform providers to take appropriate measures to address unlawful and harmful content on their platforms, noting that the latest cases were not the first civil actions it had brought against major social media companies over similar alleged violations.

The two lawsuits form part of MCMC’s ongoing efforts to protect the public, particularly children, from online threats and curb the continued circulation of content that has been subject to regulatory action and court intervention.

Malaysia unveils online safety, child protection codes

item.title: PhonePe resumes IPO preparations with up to $15 billion target
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.category: Securities and Exchange Board of India
item.description: PhonePe has reportedly restarted IPO preparations, targeting a first-quarter 2027 listing at a valuation of up to $15 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Indian digital payments company PhonePe has resumed preparations for an initial public offering that could value the Walmart-backed fintech at between $12 billion and $15 billion, according to a person familiar with the discussions cited by Reuters.

Reuters reported that PhonePe is targeting a listing in the first quarter of 2027 and is expected to file updated draft documents with the Securities and Exchange Board of India within 30 to 45 days. The source requested anonymity because the discussions are confidential.

PhonePe and Walmart did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment. No updated draft filing had been published at the time of the report, so the proposed valuation, timetable and offering structure remain subject to change.

The planned offering would be an entirely secondary share sale seeking to raise between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion, Reuters said. The size is consistent with PhonePe’s January draft prospectus, under which majority owner Walmart proposed reducing its holding by about 12 percent and investors Tiger Global and Microsoft planned to exit.

PhonePe paused its listing plans in March because of volatile global capital markets linked to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. If completed at the reported size, the transaction would be India’s largest fintech listing since Paytm’s $2.5 billion initial public offering in 2021.

The Bengaluru-based company has more than 650 million registered users. It processed nearly 11.4 billion of India’s 25.4 billion Unified Payments Interface transactions in October, according to figures cited by Reuters. The company competes with Google Pay and Paytm in the country’s digital payments market.

The report said PhonePe expects to become profitable in the next fiscal year, excluding government incentives for digital payments and any fee revenue from UPI. That projection also came from the unnamed source and has not been confirmed by the company.

India does not allow banks and fintech platforms to charge users for standard UPI transfers. A government proposal to introduce a 0.4 percent merchant fee on transactions above 2,000 rupees was deferred indefinitely after retailer opposition, Reuters reported.

PhonePe has also been expanding beyond its domestic payments base. In September, it received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates for two payment licenses, though final authorization is still required before commercial operations can begin.

India’s PhonePe gets in-principle UAE approval for two payment licenses

item.title: Singtel and GovTech plan AI-enabled smart-building platform at One Comcentre
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singtel and GovTech Singapore plan to deploy the Open Digital Platform at One Comcentre for connected building systems, robots and AI applications.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore Telecommunications (Singtel) and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) have signed a memorandum of understanding to deploy the Open Digital Platform at Singtel’s new One Comcentre development and explore artificial intelligence-enabled building applications.

The partners said in a joint announcement on Thursday that the project will combine Singtel’s 5G+ connectivity, network intelligence and AI capabilities with the platform, which was co-developed by GovTech Singapore and industrial infrastructure developer JTC Corporation. They described the development as a test bed for integrating building systems, telecommunications networks and physical AI in a single operating environment.

One Comcentre, scheduled for completion by the end of 2028, is expected to be the first building to use a version of the Open Digital Platform enhanced with telecommunications capabilities. The companies said the deployment is intended to support secure and trusted interactions among autonomous robots, AI systems and building infrastructure.

The organizations will explore uses including proactive building maintenance, deliveries, cleaning and security patrols. They also plan to develop interactive digital twins that can display real-time information about building systems and operations, helping facility teams monitor conditions and coordinate responses.

The Open Digital Platform acts as an integration layer for building systems and data. GovTech and JTC have already deployed it in Singapore’s Punggol Digital District, where it connects more than 20,000 sensors and systems, as well as at the JTC Summit and Woodlands North Coast. Its architecture has also been adapted for the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore’s maritime digital twin, according to the announcement.

The partners clarified that the platform is not itself an AI system and does not make operational decisions independently. Instead, it provides common infrastructure through which authorized applications, devices and building systems can exchange data. The word “open” refers to an interoperable and extendable architecture rather than public access to building information.

Singtel said the collaboration will also examine how its network capabilities can help different robotic systems operate within a shared building environment. That includes connectivity and coordination for machines performing tasks in common areas while building operators retain oversight of access and operations.

The project adds a telecommunications layer to Singapore’s continuing effort to apply connected data and AI across the built environment. One Comcentre will replace Singtel’s former Comcentre headquarters and is being developed as a mixed-use workplace and commercial complex on the Orchard Road corridor.

Autodesk, JTC inks deal to advance next generation of digital delivery in Singapore’s built environment
